::: {.why}
A correction you have to remember to apply is a correction you will not apply in March, so today it goes into the code that reports every Sharpe you will ever compute.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Compute a deflated Sharpe ratio from a return series, a trial count and the cross-trial Sharpe variance.
- Have your own tooling count the trials rather than trusting you to remember them.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Add `deflated_sharpe()` to qlib/stats.py, taking the observed Sharpe, the number of trials, the variance of Sharpes across trials, and the sample skewness and kurtosis. Test it against your day 51 simulation: feed it the null set and confirm the deflated value is not significant.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Build the trial counter: a small append-only log, `research_log.jsonl` in the work repo, where every backtest run writes one line with the strategy name, parameters, date and realised Sharpe. Wire it into the stats module so that running an evaluation records itself. In eleven months this file is the evidence behind the number on the front page of milestone 6.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The research log begins. Every strategy evaluation from today writes a line to research_log.jsonl, so the number of trials behind any later result is a fact you can count rather than a number you have to recall.
:::
